paraphrase_pairs.a: FAST-NUCES teaches and examines its courses in English, except language courses other than English and Islamic Studies.
paraphrase_pairs.b: English is the instruction and examination language for every course unless it is a non-English language course or Islamic Studies.

paraphrase_pairs.a: A regular semester has sixteen teaching weeks, one makeup week, and two final-exam weeks.
paraphrase_pairs.b: Regular semesters run for 16 weeks of classes followed by a makeup week and two weeks for final examinations.

paraphrase_pairs.a: One theory credit hour means one hour of classroom teaching per week during the semester.
paraphrase_pairs.b: For a theory class, each credit hour corresponds to a weekly classroom-teaching hour throughout the semester.

paraphrase_pairs.a: One laboratory credit hour is equivalent to three hours of practical or lab work each week.
paraphrase_pairs.b: Students complete three weekly hours of laboratory or practical work for every lab credit hour.

paraphrase_pairs.a: A student may enroll in no more than two courses during the summer semester.
paraphrase_pairs.b: The summer-semester registration limit is a maximum of two courses per student.

paraphrase_pairs.a: For genuine reasons, the HoD may excuse absence of up to twenty percent of the required attendance.
paraphrase_pairs.b: A department head can condone a maximum 20% absence when the student has a valid reason such as illness.

paraphrase_pairs.a: A student who does not satisfy a course's attendance rule cannot sit its final and receives an F/A grade.
paraphrase_pairs.b: Insufficient attendance makes the student ineligible for the final examination and results in an F/A in that course.

paraphrase_pairs.a: A bachelor's degree takes at least four academic years, with a normal maximum completion period of six years.
paraphrase_pairs.b: The minimum bachelor's duration is eight regular semesters; the maximum allowed time is six years.

paraphrase_pairs.a: Graduation requires a cumulative GPA of at least 2.00.
paraphrase_pairs.b: The minimum CGPA needed to graduate from an undergraduate degree is 2.00.

paraphrase_pairs.a: The grade point value for an A-minus is 3.67.
paraphrase_pairs.b: An A− earns 3.67 grade points under the grading table.

paraphrase_pairs.a: For a repeated course, CGPA uses only the most recent grade points, while the earlier grade stays on the transcript.
paraphrase_pairs.b: When a course is repeated, the latest grade-point result counts toward CGPA even though the previous attempt remains recorded.

paraphrase_pairs.a: The normal undergraduate semester load is five courses; a final-year student can take one more including FYP.
paraphrase_pairs.b: Students normally register for five courses, and a final-year student may add one extra course with the FYP included.

paraphrase_pairs.a: A course-withdrawal request needs a parent or guardian's countersignature and HoD approval.
paraphrase_pairs.b: To withdraw from a course, the student must get the application signed by a parent or guardian and approved by the Head of Department.

paraphrase_pairs.a: At least ten students must register for a summer course to be offered.
paraphrase_pairs.b: A summer course requires registration by a minimum of TEN (10) students.

paraphrase_pairs.a: The Rector's List requires an SGPA of 4.00 and at least 30 credit hours.
paraphrase_pairs.b: Students qualify for the Rector's List with a 4.00 semester GPA while completing no fewer than 30 credits.
